summary: The code is syntactically valid and calls main() at global scope, but the Simulation.run method is truncated and does not return results, causing the demo to fail (caught by try/except). Multiple required metrics and parts of the specification are not implemented or not returned. Some logic is incomplete or inconsistent with the stated task.

issues.description: Simulation.run is incomplete and does not return a results dictionary. The method ends abruptly with a stray expression 'supply_short' and no return statement.
issues.location: Simulation.run() near the end of the method
issues.solution: Complete the run() method to compute and aggregate all required metrics, then return a dictionary of results. Remove the stray 'supply_short' expression and finalize metrics (e.g., stockout_rate, compliance_in_mandated_locations, price_mean, time_to_reach_70pct) before returning.

issues.description: Because run() returns None, main() attempts to subscript a None result (res) which raises an exception. Although caught, the demo produces an error rather than valid JSON output.
issues.solution: Ensure Simulation.run returns a valid dictionary. Optionally, add a guard in main: if not res: print a minimal JSON with defaults instead of raising.

issues.description: Required metrics from the specification are missing or not output: adoption_rate_over_time (naming mismatch), time_to_reach_70pct, stockout_rate, price_mean, adoption_by_group, cascade_size_distribution, gini_adoption, cumulative_fines, and compliance_in_mandated_locations.
issues.solution: Compute and return metrics as per spec. For example: adoption_rate_over_time = series['adoption_rate']; time_to_reach_70pct = first index where adoption_rate >= 0.7; stockout_rate = stockout_retailer_days_accum / (retailer_count * days); price_mean = mean(series['average_price']); adoption_by_group stratify by demographic/income; gini_adoption = gini(group adoption rates); cumulative_fines from cumulative_fines_collected; compliance_in_mandated_locations = mean(series['compliance_in_mandated_locations_series']).

issues.description: Entity coverage deviates from the task specification. A dedicated SocialNetwork entity with connect_agents and propagate_social_influence behaviors is missing.
issues.solution: Add a SocialNetwork class (even a lightweight wrapper) to encapsulate network generation and influence propagation, or justify and document the mapping if Person.network_neighbors is intended to cover this.

issues.description: PolicyMaker entity is named PolicyAuthority and Metrics/behaviors around policy influence are partially implemented but not aligned to the required outputs (e.g., compliance_in_mandated_locations returned).
issues.location: PolicyAuthority class and Simulation.step policy handling
issues.solution: Map PolicyAuthority to PolicyMaker in naming or clearly return metrics using the specified names. Ensure mandates, enforcement, fines, and campaign outputs are surfaced in the results.

issues.description: Supply accounting is potentially inconsistent: retailers start with their own initial inventory while a central SupplyChain also has initial stock, which can lead to double-counting supply availability.
issues.solution: Initialize retailers by pulling from SupplyChain (restock at t=0) and avoid separate initial retailer stock, or reduce the SupplyChain initial stock by the sum of retailer initial inventories.

issues.description: Stockout tracking is started (stockout_retailer_days_accum) but not converted into the required metric (stockout_rate) nor returned.
issues.solution: Compute stockout_rate at the end: stockout_rate = stockout_retailer_days_accum / (retailer_count * days), and include it in the returned results.

issues.description: Compliance in mandated locations is computed only as a time series and not summarized in the results.
issues.solution: Aggregate to a final metric, e.g., compliance_in_mandated_locations = mean(compliance_in_mandated_locations_series) and include in results.

issues.description: Media/information campaign cost accounting occurs when policy_signal > 0.0, but communication_frequency and campaign_intensity interplay may not reflect ongoing costs on silent days.
issues.solution: If intended, accrue campaign cost daily when campaign_intensity > 0 and mandates are active; otherwise document this on-message-only costing.

issues.description: Observed series handling (observed_adoption_series) is not used; comments suggest intended RMSE calculation.
issues.solution: If fitting/evaluation is required, compute RMSE against observed series and return it in results; else remove the dead code/comment.

issues.description: Several functions retain a 'pass' statement followed by logic. This is harmless but confusing.
issues.location: Multiple functions (e.g., clamp, gini, poisson_sample, methods in dataclasses)
issues.solution: Remove the redundant 'pass' statements to improve clarity.
Remove unused imports to reduce clutter.
